# Active-Root Destination Amendment

In-place brownfield execution requires capability preservation evidence instead of root byte equality.

## What Happened

SALUS Pramana t9.4 superseded a sibling-directory default with explicit active-root execution. The
old VG-00 required zero root byte changes, which made any in-place implementation fail by design.

## Takeaway

When destination changes from sibling to active root, amend the full authority chain together:
output clarification, constitution boundary, plan paths, checkpoint labels, and preservation gate.
Freeze root behavior/capabilities before edits, require archive byte equality, and reconcile every
root change to a traced requirement and executable no-regression check.
